subject: Summing a parameter vector across neighbors

messages.author: 63cc02caac0434cf
messages.subject: Summing a parameter vector across neighbors
parts:
Hello, 

I am trying to calculate the sum of the parameter vector S0 across the neighbors of i like so 

Snei0[i] <- sum(S0[adj[count[i]:(count[i]+num[i]-1)]]) 

here adj[] and num[] are the vectors needed for the dcar_normal distribution. Count[] is just a constant I made that gives the proper starting index for adj[]. 

This returns the error "getSymbolicParentNodesRecurse: only scalar random indices are allowed; vector random indexing found in S0[adj[count[i]:(count[i] + num[i] - 1)]]"

Before I was using 

Snei0[i] <- inprod(NM[i,1:N],S0[1:N])

where NM is the neighborhood matrix of 0s and 1s. This worked but  is extremely slow so I thought the above might be faster. 

If you have any suggestions for how to get it working or maybe a more efficient way to calculate the sum I would be very appreciative. 

Thanks!

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Summing a parameter vector across neighbors
parts:
Hi Dirk, we  don't support the use of a vector as a set of indices in model code, which is how you are using 'adj' here. In other words, we are expecting code like: `sum(y[2:5])` or   `sum(y[idx[1]:idx[4]])` not `sum(y[idx[1:4]])`.
The error message you are getting here is misleading; I'll file an issue for us to look at improving that. 

In terms of how to work around this, a couple options that occur to me (others might have other suggestions):

1) if Snei0 is not used elsewhere in the model (i.e., if it is just a posterior functional you need), you may want to just do the calculation with the posterior samples outside of the model.

2) You could write a user-defined function that takes 'adj', 'S0', 'count' as inputs and does the calculation within the function. I think this will work but haven't tested it:

mysum <- nimbleFunction(
    run = function(S0 = double(1), adj = double(1), count = double(1), num = double(1), i = double(0)) {
        return(sum(S0[adj[count[i]:(count[i]+num[i]-1)]]) 
        returnType(double(0))
    }
)

Then in model code:

Snei0[i] <- mysum(S0, adj, count, num, i)

-Chris

parts:
Hi Chris

I noticed this exchange recently and realised that this is something that is done in various spatial models

such as the Leroux model. The  code for neighbor summming works in BUGS but gives an error in nimble

and so I followed the suggested function in your last email.

 

However this gave the following error when using nimbleModel:

 

#function:

 

mysum <- nimbleFunction(

    run = function(s = double(1), adj = double(1), cumNSC2 = double(1), i = double(0)) {

ab=cumNSC2[i]+1

i2=i+1

ac=cumNSC2[i2]

        return(sum(s[adj[ab]:adj[ac]]))

        returnType(double(0))

    }

)

 

#model:

 

LERmodel<-nimbleCode(

{for (i in 1:m){Y1998[i]~dpois(mu[i])

p.sig[i]<-step(s[i])

log(mu[i])<-log(Exp98[i])+log(theta[i])

log(theta[i])<-a0+s[i]

s[i]~dnorm(S[i],tau[i])

tau[i]<-inv.delta*(1-lam+lam*num[i])

Snei[i] <- mysum(s, adj, cumNSC2,i)

S[i]<-(lam/(1-lam+lam*num[i]))*Snei[i]}

for (i in 1:sumNumNeigh){Ws[i]<-s[adj[i]]}

inv.delta~dgamma(2,0.5)

a0~dnorm(0,tau0)

tau0~dgamma(2,0.5)

lam~dunif(0,1)

})

 

 

#nimbleModel:

 

LER<-nimbleModel(code=LERmodel,name="LER",constants=LERconsts,data=LERdata,inits=LERinits)

 

# error:

 

defining model...

Error in replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) :

  Error, hit end

In addition: Warning messages:

1: In replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) :

  Code adj was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar.  This is probably not what you want.

2: In replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) :

  Code cumNSC2 was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar.  This is probably not what you want.

 

Any thoughts on how to get round this ?

 

best

Andrew

messages.author: 35cf403e5052bfe0
messages.subject: RE: Summing a parameter vector across neighbors
parts:
Hi Chris

There seems to be some different issues with the summing of neighbors.

Some background:

The Leroux model if specified via the conditional mean and variance

has a sum of random effect values across neighbors. The original BUGS code that impemented this is given in

MacNab et al (2006) (attached). Also the code appears in Peter Congdon's book: Applied Bayesian Hierarchical Methods (2010)

 

below is the code in BUGS format: s[] is the effect and cumNSC2 is the index to neighbors vector:

##################################################################

model

{for (i in 1:m){Y1998[i]~dpois(mu[i])

p.sig[i]<-step(s[i])

log(mu[i])<-log(Exp98[i])+log(theta[i])

log(theta[i])<-a0+s[i]

s[i]~dnorm(S[i],tau[i])

tau[i]<-inv.delta*(1-lam+lam*num[i])

for (i in 1:sumNumNeigh){Ws[i]<-s[adj[i]]}

inv.delta~dgamma(2,0.5)

a0~dnorm(0,tau0)

tau0~dgamma(2,0.5)

lam~dunif(0,1)

}

#####################################################################

Alternative formulations in nimble could be imagined I guess: where the covariance is directly modelled.

 

 

There are other situations where a sum over neighbors is used in spatial or spatial -temporal models

For instance, with infectious disease models it is often reasonable to assume that transmission

occurs across neighbor boundaries from infectives arising in a previous time period. It is normal in these tyoes of models to

model the dependence on previous counts rather than on an evolving mean level.

Some code below is from a SIR model with this included, where case is the infective count and cumN is the index to the neighbors.

#####################################################################

for (i in 1:n) {

lsum[i,1]<-sum(wec[cumN[i]+1:cumN[i+1],1])

case[i,1]~dpois(mean[i,1])

log(mean[i,1])<-log(pop[i,1])+int0

for(j  in 2:T)

{

lsum[i,j]<-sum(wec[cumN[i]+1:cumN[i+1],j-1])

case[i,j]~dpois(mean[i,j])

log(mean[i,j])<-log(pop[i,j])+a0+

a_case*log(case[i,j-1]+0.0001)+

a_lsum*log(lsum[i,j]+0.001)

}

 

## and below the wec vector is set up:

 

for(k in 1:sumNumNeigh){

for (j in 1:13){

wec[k,j]<-case[adj[k],j]

}}

#################################################################

Of course in this case the lsum matrix can be pre-computed, and this would save

on computation.

I have implemented this pre-computation for nimble and this works. However I

havent as yet fixed the direct coded version.

 

BTW one small issue I have had with using nimble for these SIR models is that

when monitoring nodes it appears that the outcome data is regarded as a stochastic node and

reported in output. There is no missingness in the outcomes BTW.

I guess it is something to do with the fact we are using some pieces of the data

as conditional on others.

best

Andrew
